card.title: NAKAJIMA B5N2
card.text: Gets +1+1 when you play a card with Intel.
card.flavorText: The Nakajima B5N, nicknamed "Kate" by the Allies, was the Imperial Japanese Navy’s main torpedo bomber during the early years of WWII. It was first flown in 1937 and was considered modern and fast for its time. It was manned by a crew of three and had the ability to carry a torpedo or bombs. The B5N played a major role in early Japanese victories. It was used in the attack on Pearl Harbor, where it launched torpedoes and bombs against US battleships. It also saw action in battles such as the Coral Sea, Midway, and the Philippines, sinking or damaging several Allied ships. However, from 1943 the B5N had become outdated. It had poor armor and no self-sealing fuel tanks, making it vulnerable to enemy fighters and anti-aircraft fire. Despite this, Japan continued to use it due to delays in replacing it with the newer B6N “Jill”. The B5N remained in service until the end of the war, often used for training or in kamikaze roles. It was Japan’s most successful torpedo bomber during the war, largely due to its heavy use in the early campaigns.
